speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding gums, and a rash of tiny red spots on your skin; these symptoms suggest a problem with your blood's ability to clot. To determine the cause, please tell me your age and if you have experienced any recent bruises without injury.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The clinical presentation of frequent epistaxis, gingival bleeding, and petechiae in a 4-year-old male is highly characteristic of acute immune thrombocytopenia. REQUEST IMAGES: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with platelet count.
